newsitem.title: UK: Channel 4 planning additional digital services.
newsitem.headline: Channel 4 planning additional digital services.

text.p: Britain's Channel 4 said on Thursday that it was planning additional services for TV viewers in the multi-channel digital age.
"We are keen to extend our skills into providing extra choice for viewers," Channel 4 chief executive Michael Grade told a parliamentary select committee.

In a submission to the select committee inquiry into the BBC and the future of broadcasting, Channel 4 said it was examining the commercial feasibility of new services and how these might be delivered. Grade said these might be rolled out on cable or satellite before the launch of digital terrestrial TV.

Channel 4 forecast new digital income of five million pounds in 1999, against extra costs of 36 million pounds from its new services and digital transmission of its existing output. It said any new services would be required to break even by their fifth year of operation.

BSkyB is planning to launch digital satellite services with some 200 channels into the UK late this year. Cable operators are also likely to upgrade to digital while a terrestrial version is due to being in mid-1998.
Many in the media industry are sceptical about the prospects for digital terrestrial as it will only offer some 35 channels.
But Grade said the fact that it could be received on a standard aerial rather than via a satellite dish meant it could reach the whole of the population and should ensure its success.

Channel 4 said in its submission that the overall advertising market will continue to grow but that its audience share would fall from 10.7 percent in 1996 to around 9.0 percent in the years leading up to the expiry of its licence in 2002.
